description: We are a team of undergraduate students passionate about technology, innovation, and building creative solutions. Our interests span AI and machine learning, software development, game development, and space exploration, particularly NASA-related projects. We enjoy experimenting with new technologies, tackling challenging problems, and turning ideas into functional projects. As a team, we bring curiosity and a collaborative mindset, with a shared enthusiasm for learning and pushing our skills.
summary:
Mission Architect is an interactive desktop game where players design, launch and fly a complete space mission. They choose one of four objectives: Moon Orbiter, Mars Flyby, Earth Observation Satellite, or Asteroid Sample Return, then build a spacecraft from structures, power systems, comms, propulsion, and science instruments, and pick a launch vehicle. Live resource bars show how each choice affects budget, mass, power, and data capacity.

The mission then plays out turn by turn through launch, cruise, orbit insertion, science operations and downlink, with random events like solar flares, instrument failures and comms dropouts. Weak design choices, such as a thin power margin, make these events more damaging. Players finish with a score and a plain-language explanation of what caused success or failure.

The game addresses the challenge by turning abstract engineering trade-offs into hands-on decisions. It matters because it lets students see why real missions balance cost, mass, power and communications, and learn from failure at no cost.
details:
Mission Architect is an interactive rocket design and space mission simulation game developed using C++ and SFML 3. Players take on the role of mission architects, designing spacecraft and planning missions while balancing technical and financial constraints. The game involves selecting spacecraft components, managing payload capacity, mass, power requirements, communication systems, budget, and reliability. Players must make strategic decisions to ensure their spacecraft is suitable for its mission and can successfully progress through different mission phases.

The project aims to make introductory aerospace engineering concepts engaging and accessible through interactive gameplay. Its creative aspect lies in combining spacecraft engineering, resource management, and mission planning into a single simulation. Throughout development, we considered gameplay clarity, realistic component interactions, balanced difficulty, resource constraints, and meaningful feedback to encourage problem-solving and strategic thinking.

Technologies used: C++, SFML 3.
